rejected.title: The American Revolution
card: In the 1700s, thirteen British colonies lined the east coast of North America. Many colonists were angry that Britain taxed them while they had no members in the British Parliament.
From 1775 to 1783 the colonies fought a war against Britain. They won, and the United States of America became an independent country.
In 1776 the colonies issued the Declaration of Independence. It announced that they were breaking from Britain.

The Declaration said all people have rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. It argued that a government gets its power from the people it rules and can be changed if it fails to protect these rights.
rejected.remember: The colonies fought Britain from 1775 to 1783 and claimed rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

a.q: Which statement best describes the American Revolution?
opts: Colonies fought a war to break free from British rule
Britain fought a war to gain new colonies in America
Colonists fought to win seats in the British Parliament
Colonists fought a war against each other over taxes
a.why: The thirteen colonies fought Britain from 1775 to 1783, and in 1776 they declared independence. The Parliament option is tempting because colonists were angry at having no members in Parliament, but the colonies came to seek independence, not seats in Parliament.
a.clue: Think about who fought whom, and what the colonies became.

b.q: Why was the Declaration of Independence important to the colonists' cause?
opts: It announced their break from Britain and claimed rights
It ended the war and signed a peace with Britain
It set up a new king to rule the independent country
It gave Britain the right to tax the colonies directly
b.why: The Declaration of 1776 announced that the colonies were breaking from Britain and claimed rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. It did not end the war, which carried on until 1783.
b.clue: The Declaration came in 1776, while the war was still going.

opts: Colonies fought a war to break free from British rule
Britain fought a war to gain new colonies in America
Colonists fought to win seats in the British Parliament
Colonists fought a war against each other over taxes
a.why: The thirteen colonies fought Britain from 1775 to 1783 to become independent. The tempting option about Parliament is wrong because the colonists did not want to stay in the empire. They wanted to rule themselves.
a.clue: Think about who fought whom, and what the colonies wanted to become.

opts: It announced their break from Britain and claimed rights
It ended the war and made peace with Britain
It set up a king to rule the new country
It gave Britain the right to tax the colonies
b.why: The Declaration of 1776 announced that the colonies were breaking from Britain and claimed rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. It did not end the war, which carried on until 1783.
b.clue: The Declaration came in 1776, while the war was still going.

problems.detail: The why says flatly that 'the colonists did not want to stay in the empire'. Many colonists were Loyalists, and when fighting began in 1775 many Patriots still sought their rights within the empire. Independence was not declared until 1776. Say 'the colonies came to seek independence' or 'many colonists wanted to rule themselves' instead.
